primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: NF1 encodes neurofibromin, a tumor suppressor that down-regulates RAS signaling; affected individuals inherit one altered NF1 copy and tumors arise after somatic loss of the remaining normal copy in susceptible cells.
vignette: A 13-year-old boy has multiple café-au-lait macules, axillary freckling, and several soft cutaneous neurofibromas. His mother has similar findings.
lead: Which molecular mechanism best explains tumor formation in this disorder?
correct: Loss of both functional copies of a tumor-suppressor gene in tumor-forming cells
distractors: Constitutive activation of a receptor tyrosine kinase from one inherited allele only
Trinucleotide repeat expansion causing gene silencing
Defective nucleotide excision repair after ultraviolet exposure
distractor_notes: Constitutive activation from one inherited oncogenic allele does not match the NF1 tumor-suppressor mechanism in which tumor formation requires loss of the remaining functional NF1 copy in affected cells.
Mitochondrial heteroplasmy does not match the NF1 tumor-suppressor mechanism in which tumor formation requires alteration of both NF1 copies in affected cells.
Repeat-expansion gene silencing does not match the NF1 tumor-suppressor mechanism in which tumor formation requires alteration of both NF1 copies in affected cells.
Defective nucleotide excision repair does not match the NF1 tumor-suppressor mechanism in which tumor formation requires alteration of both NF1 copies in affected cells.
key_expl: NF1 tumor formation follows tumor-suppressor biology: a germline NF1 variant is followed by somatic loss of the remaining functional allele in affected cells.
objective: Explain NF1 tumor formation using the two-hit tumor-suppressor model.

sources.title: Neurofibromatosis type 1
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes café-au-lait macules, axillary/groin freckling, neurofibromas, autosomal dominant inheritance, and second-hit loss of the remaining NF1 copy in tumor cells.

sources.title: NF1 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes neurofibromin as a tumor suppressor involved in controlling cell growth through RAS-related signaling.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: TSC1 and TSC2 encode hamartin and tuberin, tumor suppressors that restrain cell growth; loss of both functional copies in individual cells permits hamartoma formation in multiple organs.
vignette: A 9-year-old child has seizures, hypopigmented macules, facial angiofibromas, cortical tubers, and bilateral renal angiomyolipomas.
lead: Which cellular function is most directly lost?
correct: Tumor-suppressor restraint of cell growth by the hamartin-tuberin complex
distractors: DNA mismatch repair of replication errors
distractor_notes: DNA mismatch repair does not match the demonstrated loss of hamartin-tuberin tumor-suppressor control of cell growth.
CFTR chloride transport does not match the demonstrated loss of hamartin-tuberin tumor-suppressor control of cell growth.
Type I collagen synthesis does not match the demonstrated loss of hamartin-tuberin tumor-suppressor control of cell growth.
Peroxisomal fatty-acid transport does not match the demonstrated loss of hamartin-tuberin tumor-suppressor control of cell growth.
key_expl: TSC1/TSC2 proteins act together as tumor suppressors; loss of hamartin/tuberin permits uncontrolled cell growth and benign tumors across organs.
objective: Link TSC manifestations to loss of hamartin-tuberin tumor-suppressor function.

sources.title: Tuberous sclerosis complex
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes benign tumors in brain, kidneys, heart, and skin and identifies TSC1/TSC2 as tumor-suppressor genes regulating cell growth.

sources.title: TSC2 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics explains that tuberin loss after second-hit TSC2 variants permits uncontrolled growth and tumor formation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: VHL tumor-suppressor loss prevents normal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factors, allowing HIF accumulation and increased expression of growth and angiogenic programs.
vignette: A 32-year-old man has a retinal hemangioblastoma and clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. His father had a cerebellar hemangioblastoma. Germline testing shows a pathogenic VHL variant.
lead: Which intracellular protein is expected to accumulate when VHL function is lost?
distractor_notes: Retinoblastoma protein is not the oxygen-sensing degradation target that accumulates when VHL function is lost.
Dystrophin is not the oxygen-sensing degradation target that accumulates when VHL function is lost.
Fibrillin-1 is not the oxygen-sensing degradation target that accumulates when VHL function is lost.
Hexosaminidase A is not the oxygen-sensing degradation target that accumulates when VHL function is lost.
key_expl: VHL protein participates in targeting HIF for degradation; loss of VHL allows HIF accumulation and inappropriate angiogenic/growth signaling.
objective: Explain VHL-associated tumor biology through failure of HIF degradation.
clues: retinal hemangioblastoma with clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
autosomal-dominant family pattern with pathogenic VHL variant

sources.title: Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes VHL as an autosomal dominant tumor-predisposition syndrome with hemangioblastomas and renal tumors caused by VHL tumor-suppressor dysfunction.

sources.title: VHL gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics explains that VHL protein helps target HIF for breakdown and that VHL loss permits HIF accumulation and excess angiogenic/growth signaling.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Abnormal regulation of imprinted growth-control genes on chromosome 11p15 shifts expression toward fetal overgrowth, producing macrosomia, macroglossia, abdominal-wall defects, hemihyperplasia, and tumor predisposition.
vignette: A newborn has macrosomia, macroglossia, an omphalocele, neonatal hypoglycemia, and asymmetric enlargement of the right side of the body.
lead: Which genetic principle best explains this syndrome?
correct: Abnormal genomic imprinting of growth-regulating genes
distractors: X-linked recessive inheritance from a carrier mother
Somatic chromosomal translocation confined to a leukemia clone
distractor_notes: Mitochondrial maternal inheritance does not match the abnormal regulation of imprinted growth-control genes on chromosome 11 that underlies this phenotype.
X-linked recessive inheritance does not match the abnormal regulation of imprinted growth-control genes on chromosome 11 that underlies this phenotype.
Trinucleotide repeat anticipation does not match the abnormal regulation of imprinted growth-control genes on chromosome 11 that underlies this phenotype.
A somatic change confined to a tumor clone cannot explain a congenital multisystem overgrowth phenotype caused by abnormal imprinting of chromosome 11 growth-control genes.
key_expl: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is an overgrowth syndrome caused most often by abnormal imprinting/regulation at chromosome 11p15.
objective: Recognize BWS and link its overgrowth phenotype to genomic imprinting.

sources.title: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes macrosomia, macroglossia, abdominal-wall defects, hemihyperplasia, hypoglycemia, tumor risk, and imprinting abnormalities on chromosome 11.

sources.title: CDKN1C gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes CDKN1C as a growth-control gene in the imprinted chromosome 11p15 region and one cause of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Gain-of-function or prolonged activation of proteins in the RAS/MAPK pathway disrupts normal regulation of cell growth, differentiation, and migration, producing a RASopathy with characteristic facial, cardiac, skeletal, and growth findings.
vignette: A 7-year-old boy has short stature, hypertelorism, low-set ears, a webbed neck, pectus deformity, and pulmonic stenosis. Karyotype is 46,XY.
lead: Which signaling pathway is most likely dysregulated?
distractor_notes: JAK2-centered erythropoietin signaling does not match the RAS/MAPK pathway dysregulation that MedlinePlus identifies in Noonan syndrome.
Hedgehog-pathway processing does not match the RAS/MAPK pathway dysregulation that MedlinePlus identifies in Noonan syndrome.
CFTR chloride-channel function does not match the RAS/MAPK pathway dysregulation that MedlinePlus identifies in Noonan syndrome.
Terminal complement signaling does not match the RAS/MAPK pathway dysregulation that MedlinePlus identifies in Noonan syndrome.
key_expl: Noonan syndrome is a RASopathy caused by variants that prolong or dysregulate RAS/MAPK signaling.
objective: Link Noonan syndrome to abnormal RAS/MAPK pathway signaling.
clues: pulmonic stenosis with normal male karyotype

sources.title: Noonan syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Noonan syndrome features and identifies it as a RASopathy caused by prolonged activation of RAS/MAPK signaling.

sources.title: PTPN11 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes PTPN11 as a RAS/MAPK signaling gene and a major genetic cause of Noonan syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Expansion of the FMR1 CGG repeat to a full mutation (>200 repeats) causes methylation and silencing of FMR1, leading to deficiency of FMRP and impaired neuronal/synaptic function.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy has intellectual disability, autism-like behaviors, a long narrow face, large ears, and macroorchidism. His maternal uncle has similar cognitive disability.
lead: Which molecular change is most likely?
correct: CGG repeat expansion causing FMR1 silencing
distractors: CAG expansion causing a toxic huntingtin protein
distractor_notes: HTT CAG expansion causes Huntington disease.
FXN GAA expansion causes Friedreich ataxia.
DMPK CTG expansion causes myotonic dystrophy.
SMN1 deletion causes spinal muscular atrophy.
key_expl: Fragile X syndrome is caused in nearly all cases by expansion of the FMR1 CGG repeat beyond 200 copies, which silences FMR1 and reduces FMRP.
objective: Link the characteristic phenotype of fragile X syndrome to FMR1 CGG expansion and gene silencing.
clues: intellectual/autism phenotype with long face/large ears

sources.title: Fragile X syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes the phenotype and explains that >200 CGG repeats in FMR1 silence the gene and reduce FMRP.

sources.title: FMR1 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes FMR1 CGG repeat expansion and silencing in fragile X syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: OTC deficiency blocks conversion of carbamoyl phosphate plus ornithine to citrulline in the hepatic urea cycle, impairing nitrogen disposal and causing hyperammonemia.
vignette: A 3-day-old boy becomes lethargic and tachypneic after protein feeding. Plasma ammonia is markedly elevated, glucose is normal, and there is no metabolic acidosis.
lead: Which urea-cycle reaction is directly impaired?
correct: Carbamoyl phosphate plus ornithine to citrulline
distractors: Ammonia plus bicarbonate to carbamoyl phosphate
distractor_notes: Citrulline-to-argininosuccinate is catalyzed by argininosuccinate synthetase.
Argininosuccinate cleavage requires argininosuccinate lyase.
Arginine cleavage to urea and ornithine requires arginase.
Carbamoyl-phosphate synthesis is catalyzed by CPS1 upstream of OTC.
key_expl: Ornithine transcarbamylase catalyzes carbamoyl phosphate + ornithine → citrulline; deficiency blocks urea-cycle nitrogen disposal and causes hyperammonemia.
objective: Identify the specific urea-cycle reaction catalyzed by OTC.

sources.title: OTC gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics states that ornithine transcarbamylase catalyzes the reaction of carbamoyl phosphate and ornithine to form citrulline in the urea cycle.

sources.title: Urea Cycle Disorders
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes urea-cycle defects as causes of toxic ammonia accumulation due to impaired nitrogen disposal.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Most classic Rett syndrome results from de novo pathogenic MECP2 variants that disrupt regulation of gene activity and neuronal function, producing developmental regression in girls after an initially normal early period.
vignette: A 20-month-old girl had normal early development but now has lost purposeful hand use and spoken words. She develops repetitive hand-wringing movements, gait difficulty, and decelerating head growth.
lead: Which gene is most likely altered?
distractor_notes: FMR1 repeat expansion causes fragile X syndrome, usually with developmental delay rather than classic regression/hand stereotypies.
NF1 variants cause neurofibromatosis type 1.
TSC2 variants cause tuberous sclerosis complex.
DMD variants cause dystrophinopathy.
key_expl: Classic Rett syndrome in girls is caused in almost all cases by MECP2 variants and features developmental regression with loss of hand skills/language and stereotypic hand movements.
objective: Recognize Rett syndrome from developmental regression and MECP2-associated neurologic phenotype.
clues: loss of purposeful hand use with hand-wringing

sources.title: Rett syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Rett syndrome as an MECP2-related disorder, usually in girls, with developmental regression and characteristic neurologic manifestations.

sources.title: MECP2 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes MeCP2 regulation of gene activity/neuronal function and MECP2 variants causing Rett syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Biallelic DHCR7 deficiency impairs the final step of cholesterol synthesis, reducing cholesterol and increasing 7-dehydrocholesterol, which disrupts embryonic development and multiple organ systems.
vignette: A newborn has growth restriction, microcephaly, syndactyly of the second and third toes, ambiguous genitalia, and congenital heart disease. Plasma cholesterol is low and 7-dehydrocholesterol is elevated.
correct: Final reduction step in endogenous cholesterol synthesis
distractors: Transport of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes
distractor_notes: PAH deficiency causes phenylketonuria.
BCKD deficiency causes maple syrup urine disease.
Peroxisomal VLCFA transport defects cause X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease.
key_expl: DHCR7 encodes 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase, which catalyzes the final step in cholesterol synthesis; deficiency causes Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome.
objective: Link low cholesterol plus congenital anomalies to DHCR7 deficiency in the final cholesterol-synthesis step.

sources.title: Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes congenital multisystem abnormalities and DHCR7 deficiency affecting the final step of cholesterol production.

sources.title: DHCR7 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase and its role in the final conversion step of cholesterol synthesis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: GALNS or GLB1 deficiency impairs lysosomal glycosaminoglycan degradation; accumulated GAGs especially damage cartilage and bone, producing severe skeletal abnormalities while intelligence is often preserved.
vignette: A 9-year-old child has short-trunk dwarfism, pectus carinatum, genu valgum, joint laxity, and corneal clouding. Intelligence is normal. Testing shows deficient N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase activity.
lead: Which substrate accumulates because of this enzyme deficiency?
distractor_notes: GM2 accumulates in Tay-Sachs disease.
Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher disease.
Sphingomyelin accumulates in acid sphingomyelinase deficiency.
VLCFAs accumulate in peroxisomal disorders such as X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
key_expl: MPS IV is a lysosomal storage disorder in which GALNS/GLB1 defects prevent degradation of GAGs; GALNS normally removes sulfate from keratan sulfate.
objective: Link Morquio skeletal disease to lysosomal accumulation of keratan-sulfate–containing glycosaminoglycans.
clues: severe skeletal dysplasia with preserved cognition

sources.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type IV
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes MPS IV as a lysosomal storage disorder from GALNS/GLB1 deficiency with GAG accumulation, particularly affecting bone.

sources.title: GALNS gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics states that GALNS encodes a lysosomal enzyme that removes sulfate from keratan sulfate during GAG degradation.
